document_front_matter: Overarching arcs, location boards, quest types, difficulty, artifact logic, faction stakes, and 5e-ready table hooks

Prepared from the uploaded Belavadös DOCX quest packets and the gods, alignments, races, and pantheon compendium. The goal is not to replace the underlying data; it is to make each record easier to run as high-fantasy dark horror steampunk D&D 5e.

Generation note: the faction packet DOCX contains faction systems, arc summaries, and sample quest records, and it states that the full 717-record database lives in separate JSON/CSV/Markdown files not included in this upload. This document therefore preserves and improves the faction data that is actually present in the uploaded DOCX.
Quick Navigation: • How to Run This Quest Hook Compendium
• Quest Hooks by Overarching Arc, Location, Type, and Difficulty
How to Run This Quest Hook Compendium: Treat each record as a table-ready hook, not a locked plot. Start with the hook, show at least one living witness or visible consequence, then let the party choose whether they investigate, negotiate, engineer a ritual solution, or fight.

Every quest should support the three pillars of D&D play: social interaction, exploration, and combat. A high-level party should be able to use class features, spells, tool proficiencies, social leverage, and brute force in different combinations.

For mysteries and artifact investigations, do not hide progress behind one roll. Give at least three different clues for any conclusion the party must reach: one physical clue, one witness or social clue, and one magical, historical, or faction clue.

For horror, reveal cost before consequence. Ichor shortcuts can save time but create debt, mutation, false memory, divine-prison leakage, or blackmail. Artifacts should feel tempting because they solve something immediately while making the campaign worse later.
Use Belavadös deadlines as atmosphere and legal/religious pressure. Use real table time for scheduling, initiative, and session pacing.
Artifact Logic for Belavadös: Artifacts in this setting do not need to be ornate. A broken mirror, pipe, rope, unfinished manuscript, ring, journal, suit of armor, or tool can become an artifact when a sacrifice, oath, murder, miracle, dragon-breath, lich-ritual, god-prison tremor, or perfectly witnessed moment catches inside it.
Pantheon and Alignment Reference: Use creator-god traditions as flavor pressure, not moral determinism. A race, bloodline, faction, or artifact can echo a god without forcing an NPC or player character to obey that god.
Quest Hooks by Overarching Arc, Location: Each compact card keeps the underlying quest identity, location, pantheon/faction pressure, deadline, and 5e logic. Sorting order is Overarching Arc -> Province -> Type -> Difficulty. Each hook is written to support social, exploration, and combat/containment play without requiring a separate crafting or tradeskill subsystem.
Named NPC Reference: Named NPCs from the uploaded files are preserved as names, pronouns, origin locations, and roles. Use them as quest patrons, witnesses, rivals, workers, protected targets, or consequences rather than replacing them with generic job titles.
Faction Framework Reference: Faction quests work best when each faction has a public goal, a hidden truth, a reward it can provide, and a line it will cross. Use these as recurring pressure engines for the hooks above.
Research Sources Used: These sources were used as design guidance only. The quest content remains Belavadös-specific and drawn from the uploaded DOCX materials.
Final Running Checklist: • Open with a visible crisis, not a lore lecture.
• Give three clue paths to every required conclusion.
• Name the faction that benefits if the party does nothing.
• Make the artifact useful, dangerous, and morally expensive.
• Track consequences through NPCs, permits, rumors, transit, sanctuary access, and alignment axes.
• Never make tool proficiency mandatory; let it grant advantage, alternate clues, reduced time, safer repairs, or better rewards.

five_e_conversion_rules_applied.Applied 5e table logic: Converted into dangerous fieldwork, hazardous expeditions, escort logistics, evidence audits, ritual setup, repair under pressure, social bargaining, or survival challenges. Tool proficiencies can help, but no separate tradeskill subsystem is required.

A character can sense that an item is extraordinary by handling it. Identify or focused short-rest study can reveal properties. Dangerous Belavadös artifacts should reveal motives and costs through scenes, not only item rules.

Use attunement for items that change the bearer, stack major combat/social power, grant ongoing spell-like effects, or bind to a curse. Artifacts in these hooks are usually story objects; purified remnants can become rare, very rare, legendary, or artifact-tier rewards if the DM wants.
Level 8 is the campaign floor. Low fieldwork fits levels 8-9, moderate 9-11, high 10-12, severe 12-14, and extreme 14-16 unless the quest itself states otherwise.
Use reputation, permits, lodging, warrants, witnesses, safehouse access, transit priority, rare contacts, and legal leverage. Money and magic items are optional, not the only reward.
The four axes are reputation levers rather than punishment. Altruism, Lawfulness, Cooperation, and Honor should move based on visible choices and who benefits or suffers.

preserved_roles.Preserved role and table use: Faerie obsessive apprentice gatherer, guild errand-spark, and adorable disaster magnet (Or'lythae, El'dravire Riverrealm; pronouns: they/them). Use Qho as the recurring innocent instigator. They never ask for murder; they ask for samples, observations, permits, and proof that adults are overreacting.

Human field captain of the Thornwillow Guard and practical protector of dangerous supply routes (Sylvanreach, Eldermere; pronouns: she/her). Use Mira to turn guard work into rescue logistics, bridge repairs, patrol-map ethics, and civilian protection instead of simple monster hunting.

Ombrask Arcane Shade Militia commander specializing in evidence wards, midnight warrants, and containment logistics (Eldryssar, Vaelmyrith; pronouns: they/them). Use Veyl to make law, secrecy, and arcane evidence dangerous without making the party villains by default.

factions.Public goal: Defend settlements, repair transit lifelines, and keep hungry gods from becoming excuses for tyranny.
factions.Hidden truth: Some cells quietly move refugees away from ichor debts and forged death-ledgers.

factions.Public goal: Protect Belavadös from rogue constructs, uncontrolled ichor engines, and divine-prison breaches.
factions.Hidden truth: Their purity laws hide a terror of created people and souls housed in engineered bodies.

factions.Public goal: Expose abusive ledgers, hide endangered witnesses, and free people mislabeled as property.
factions.Hidden truth: Some cells erase memories without consent when they decide secrecy matters more than personhood.

factions.Public goal: Solve plague, famine, and magical instability through regulated research.
factions.Hidden truth: Their clean laboratories hide personhood theft, forced replacement, and soul architecture experiments.

factions.Public goal: Recover stolen identities, solve murders, and protect people whose memories have been tampered with.
factions.Hidden truth: The Inquest sells sanitized memories to nobles when survival requires compromise.

factions.Public goal: Keep ocean settlements alive through fog seasons, monster migrations, and divine seal tremors.
factions.Hidden truth: Their old families know which lighthouse bells are actually prison alarms.

factions.Public goal: Protect people from surface collapse with regulated underground infrastructure.
factions.Hidden truth: Some experiments measure obedience, desperation, and ichor dependency more than safety.

factions.Public goal: Make profit, hold territory, and turn terror into spectacle.
factions.Hidden truth: The league is a recruitment mask for old god-cults and debtor armies.

quest_hooks.hook: Vaelunthir Harbor Compact asks the party to secure rare materials, observations, witnesses, or ward components near Vaelunthir. This is no longer a crafting errand; it is a 5e expedition where survival choices, permits, and endangered workers matter.

quest_hooks.title: Skarnfell Frost-Mine Pattern
quest_hooks.overarching_arc: Cold Thread Shawl of the Deep Clans
quest_hooks.overarching_arc_heading: Cold Thread Shawl of the Deep Clans (6 hooks)
quest_hooks.deadline: use settlement clock and patron deadline.
quest_hooks.hook: Skarnfell Underdeep Compact asks the party to secure rare materials, observations, witnesses, or ward components near Skarnfell. This is no longer a crafting errand; it is a 5e expedition where survival choices, permits, and endangered workers matter.
quest_hooks.objective: Use ability checks, tool proficiencies, spells, and roleplay to retrieve the objective without turning local laborers into bait. The material focus is armorsmithing, but success should come from player choices, not a separate tradeskill system.
quest_hooks.complication: The worksite is hazardous terrain: boiling vents, flood locks, unstable scaffolds, mine gas, cursed fog, or wrong-time sky tides. A direct fight is possible, but a clever crafting solution should reduce the encounter budget or remove one wave
quest_hooks.five_e_reward: Run as a 5e group check: 3 successes before 2 failures for low/moderate, 5 before 3 for high/severe, plus initiative if the hazard becomes active. Reward: Field formula: Brasscap Mushroom Field Method. Convert this to 5e as a consumable boon, advantage on a future related check, temporary equipment access, a permit, faction favor, or a contact rather than a standalone crafting subsystem.
quest_hooks.artifact_or_chassis: skill challenge, escort, hazardous exploration, negotiation, or set-piece fight A normal job becomes heroic because the party protects people, truth, and civic infrastructure while handling dangerous materials.
quest_hooks.alignment: Lawfulness +250 for legal permits; Cooperation +250 for shared credit with local guilds

Convert this to 5e as a consumable boon, advantage on a future related check, temporary equipment access, a permit, faction favor, or a contact rather than a standalone crafting subsystem.

quest_hooks.title: Question the Ledger-Bound Quarantine
quest_hooks.hook: Wildbloom reports that a household secret will become public law.
quest_hooks.objective: Recover a person, relic, or ledger before the ichor-black market can auction it. Frame the scene with at least one social route, one exploration/proof route, and one combat or containment route so the level-8+ party can choose how ugly the truth becomes.
quest_hooks.complication: The evidence is alive, frightened, and legally property under a corrupt charter. Ichor dependency should make the easy answer costly: fast magic draws debt, false memories, mutation risk, or faction leverage.
quest_hooks.five_e_reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 16; Arcana/Religion/History DC 17; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 18; crisis save DC 17. Reward: Mercy, lawful proof, quiet containment, public exposure, or faction betrayal all change the aftermath. Track changes through faction reputation, household consequences, public rumor, and service relationships; flags: ["faction_reputation", "household_consequence", "public_rumor", "service_relationship"].
quest_hooks.artifact_or_chassis: story quest, faction arc, add-on arc, or radiant template that plugs into local schedules Ichor is the civic miracle and the civic horror: every solution should expose who profits from dependency.
quest_hooks.alignment: Resolve with mercy, lawful proof, quiet containment, public exposure, or faction betrayal; each shifts Altruism, Lawfulness, Cooperation, and Honor differently.

quest_hooks.title: Vorakmar Last Cart
quest_hooks.deadline: use settlement clock and patron deadline.
quest_hooks.hook: Vorakmar Underdeep Compact asks the party to secure rare materials, observations, witnesses, or ward components near Vorakmar. This is no longer a crafting errand; it is a 5e expedition where survival choices, permits, and endangered workers matter.
quest_hooks.objective: Use ability checks, tool proficiencies, spells, and roleplay to retrieve the objective without turning local laborers into bait. The material focus is carpentry, but success should come from player choices, not a separate tradeskill system.
quest_hooks.complication: The objective sits in a resource pocket watched by predators, cult scouts, bandits, or possessed machinery. A direct fight is possible, but a clever crafting solution should reduce the encounter budget or remove one wave entirely
quest_hooks.five_e_reward: Run as a 5e group check: 3 successes before 2 failures for low/moderate, 5 before 3 for high/severe, plus initiative if the hazard becomes active. Reward: Field formula: Emberstone Field Method. Convert this to 5e as a consumable boon, advantage on a future related check, temporary equipment access, a permit, faction favor, or a contact rather than a standalone crafting subsystem.
quest_hooks.artifact_or_chassis: skill challenge, escort, hazardous exploration, negotiation, or set-piece fight A normal job becomes heroic because the party protects people, truth, and civic infrastructure while handling dangerous materials.
quest_hooks.alignment: Altruism +250 if workers are protected before profit; Honor -250 if evidence is falsified

quest_hooks.overarching_arc: Mischief in the Abandoned Relay Mine
quest_hooks.overarching_arc_heading: Mischief in the Abandoned Relay Mine (5 hooks)
quest_hooks.deadline: use settlement clock and patron deadline.
quest_hooks.hook: Rivenwild Greenwatch Circle asks the party to secure rare materials, observations, witnesses, or ward components near Rivenwild. This is no longer a crafting errand; it is a 5e expedition where survival choices, permits, and endangered workers matter.
quest_hooks.objective: Use ability checks, tool proficiencies, spells, and roleplay to retrieve the objective without turning local laborers into bait. The material focus is blacksmithing, but success should come from player choices, not a separate tradeskill system.
quest_hooks.complication: This is an escort-crafting job: NPC workers can finish the task faster if the party controls noise, light, fear, and morale. A direct fight is possible, but a clever crafting solution should reduce the encounter budget or remove one wave entirely
quest_hooks.five_e_reward: Run as a 5e group check: 3 successes before 2 failures for low/moderate, 5 before 3 for high/severe, plus initiative if the hazard becomes active. Reward: Field formula: Storm Ore Field Method. Convert this to 5e as a consumable boon, advantage on a future related check, temporary equipment access, a permit, faction favor, or a contact rather than a standalone crafting subsystem.
quest_hooks.artifact_or_chassis: skill challenge, escort, hazardous exploration, negotiation, or set-piece fight A normal job becomes heroic because the party protects people, truth, and civic infrastructure while handling dangerous materials.
quest_hooks.alignment: Altruism +250 for rescue work; Honor +250 for returning rare materials instead of pocketing them

quest_hooks.raw_text_exact_from_docx: BAQ-A186 - Seal Marrowlit Dhoti of the Last Contract | Vireluna, Lun’tharavé | Level 9 (standard high-fantasy threat) | Patron: local civic, temple, or containment authority | Deity/Pantheon: Horundar | Deadline: Valkhaday Thoryn-Rahek 16 first bell. Hook: Vireluna reports that Marrowlit Dhoti is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely. Objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it. Complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage. 5e / reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 15; Arcana/Religion/History DC 16; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 17; crisis save DC 16. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Armory of Soft Apocalypse; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item. Artifact or chassis: wondrous item or cursed oddity; identify reveals function, but containment reveals motive bound by a bearer who sacrificed comfort, identity, or a name; its omen is shaped by Horundar, master of storms, seas, earthquakes, floods, and untamed elemental force. Alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

quest_hooks.raw_text_exact_from_docx: BAQ-E017 - The Winter Core That Remembered Too Much | Vaelynor, Earrorim | Level 14 (severe province threat) | Patron: local civic, temple, or containment authority | Deity/Pantheon: Marduthor | Deadline: Anubaday Bastve'enlil 9 gravewatch. Hook: Vaelynor reports that The Winter Core That Remembered Too Much is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely. Objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it. Complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage. 5e / reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 20; Arcana/Religion/History DC 21; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 22; crisis save DC 21. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Blackledger Reliquary; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item. Artifact or chassis: wearable wondrous item, ring, armor, or restraint; attunement recommended because the object changes the bearer an ordinary object turned artifact by sacrifice, public terror, godly attention, or a moment that refused to end; its omen is shaped by Marduthor, divine smith and architect of invention, craft, metalwork, and underground halls. Alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

quest_hooks.hook: Murethash reports that Star-River Wings is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely.
quest_hooks.objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it.
quest_hooks.complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage.
quest_hooks.five_e_reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 17; Arcana/Religion/History DC 18; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 19; crisis save DC 18. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Blackledger Reliquary; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item.
quest_hooks.artifact_or_chassis: wondrous item or cursed oddity; identify reveals function, but containment reveals motive an ordinary object turned artifact by sacrifice, public terror, godly attention, or a moment that refused to end; its omen is shaped by Freyseth, mistress of crossroads, curses, planar mysteries, and supernatural bloodlines.
quest_hooks.alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

Hook: Lunebriar reports that Void-Tuned Lightbulb is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely. Objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it. Complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage. 5e / reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 17; Arcana/Religion/History DC 18; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 19; crisis save DC 18. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Blackledger Reliquary; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item. Artifact or chassis: wondrous item or cursed oddity; identify reveals function, but containment reveals motive made when a single impossible sight was caught in glass, brass, ink, or smoke; its omen is shaped by Eirzunet, creator of cursed shadows, transformations, forbidden magic, and eerie twilight races. Alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

quest_hooks.raw_text_exact_from_docx: BAQ-A030 - Seal Salt-Crowned Manuscript of the Quiet Crown | Faelvyrûn, Iazethas | Level 8 (standard high-fantasy threat) | Patron: local civic, temple, or containment authority | Deity/Pantheon: Nefarokir | Deadline: Valkhaday Bastve'enlil 4 first bell. Hook: Faelvyrûn reports that Salt-Crowned Manuscript is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely. Objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it. Complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage. 5e / reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 14; Arcana/Religion/History DC 15; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 16; crisis save DC 15. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Blackledger Reliquary; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item. Artifact or chassis: wondrous item focused on divination, illusion, memory, or testimony made when a confession, dying breath, or court record was trapped in an ordinary object; its omen is shaped by Nefarokir, lord of death, the underworld, spirits, and the forgotten dead. Alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

quest_hooks.hook: Meadowlight Expanse reports that Lantern-Black Janus Coin is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely.
quest_hooks.objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it.
quest_hooks.complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage.
quest_hooks.five_e_reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 18; Arcana/Religion/History DC 19; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 20; crisis save DC 19. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Blackledger Reliquary; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item.
quest_hooks.artifact_or_chassis: wondrous item or cursed oddity; identify reveals function, but containment reveals motive an ordinary object turned artifact by sacrifice, public terror, godly attention, or a moment that refused to end; its omen is shaped by Anubaldir, titan of endurance, burden, colossal strength, and primal might.
quest_hooks.alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

quest_hooks.raw_text_exact_from_docx: BAQ-A287 - Seal Brassbound Archive Diorama of the Drowned Forge | Heth'vára, Drakmorren | Level 10 (hard regional threat) | Patron: local civic, temple, or containment authority | Deity/Pantheon: Sigrananna | Deadline: Marduday Nefarokir 3 gravewatch. Hook: Heth'vára reports that Brassbound Archive Diorama is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely. Objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it. Complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage. 5e / reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 16; Arcana/Religion/History DC 17; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 18; crisis save DC 17. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Settlement-Ending Machines; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item. Artifact or chassis: wondrous item or cursed oddity; identify reveals function, but containment reveals motive god-made or temple-engineered to pin a divine-prison seal in place; its omen is shaped by Sigrananna, mistress of forests, moonlight, wilderness, and graceful hunters. Alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

heading_path.heading_1: 5e Conversion Rules Applied

rows: Converted into dangerous fieldwork, hazardous expeditions, escort logistics, evidence audits, ritual setup, repair under pressure, social bargaining, or survival challenges. Tool proficiencies can help, but no separate tradeskill subsystem is required.

A character can sense that an item is extraordinary by handling it. Identify or focused short-rest study can reveal properties. Dangerous Belavadös artifacts should reveal motives and costs through scenes, not only item rules.

Use attunement for items that change the bearer, stack major combat/social power, grant ongoing spell-like effects, or bind to a curse. Artifacts in these hooks are usually story objects; purified remnants can become rare, very rare, legendary, or artifact-tier rewards if the DM wants.
Level 8 is the campaign floor. Low fieldwork fits levels 8-9, moderate 9-11, high 10-12, severe 12-14, and extreme 14-16 unless the quest itself states otherwise.
Use reputation, permits, lodging, warrants, witnesses, safehouse access, transit priority, rare contacts, and legal leverage. Money and magic items are optional, not the only reward.
The four axes are reputation levers rather than punishment. Altruism, Lawfulness, Cooperation, and Honor should move based on visible choices and who benefits or suffers.

heading_path.heading_1: Faction Framework Reference

rows: Defend settlements, repair transit lifelines, and keep hungry gods from becoming excuses for tyranny.
Some cells quietly move refugees away from ichor debts and forged death-ledgers.
Protect Belavadös from rogue constructs, uncontrolled ichor engines, and divine-prison breaches.
Their purity laws hide a terror of created people and souls housed in engineered bodies.
Expose abusive ledgers, hide endangered witnesses, and free people mislabeled as property.
Some cells erase memories without consent when they decide secrecy matters more than personhood.
Solve plague, famine, and magical instability through regulated research.
Their clean laboratories hide personhood theft, forced replacement, and soul architecture experiments.
Recover stolen identities, solve murders, and protect people whose memories have been tampered with.
The Inquest sells sanitized memories to nobles when survival requires compromise.
Keep ocean settlements alive through fog seasons, monster migrations, and divine seal tremors.
Their old families know which lighthouse bells are actually prison alarms.
Protect people from surface collapse with regulated underground infrastructure.
Some experiments measure obedience, desperation, and ichor dependency more than safety.
Make profit, hold territory, and turn terror into spectacle.

heading_path.heading_1: How to Run This Quest Hook Compendium

source_document_blocks.text: Treat each record as a table-ready hook, not a locked plot. Start with the hook, show at least one living witness or visible consequence, then let the party choose whether they investigate, negotiate, engineer a ritual solution, or fight.

heading_path.heading_1: How to Run This Quest Hook Compendium

source_document_blocks.text: Every quest should support the three pillars of D&D play: social interaction, exploration, and combat. A high-level party should be able to use class features, spells, tool proficiencies, social leverage, and brute force in different combinations.

heading_path.heading_1: How to Run This Quest Hook Compendium

source_document_blocks.text: For mysteries and artifact investigations, do not hide progress behind one roll. Give at least three different clues for any conclusion the party must reach: one physical clue, one witness or social clue, and one magical, historical, or faction clue.

heading_path.heading_1: How to Run This Quest Hook Compendium

source_document_blocks.text: For horror, reveal cost before consequence. Ichor shortcuts can save time but create debt, mutation, false memory, divine-prison leakage, or blackmail. Artifacts should feel tempting because they solve something immediately while making the campaign worse later.

heading_path.heading_1: How to Run This Quest Hook Compendium

source_document_blocks.text: Use Belavadös deadlines as atmosphere and legal/religious pressure. Use real table time for scheduling, initiative, and session pacing.

heading_path.heading_1: 5e Conversion Rules Applied
5e Conversion Rules Applied

rows: Converted into dangerous fieldwork, hazardous expeditions, escort logistics, evidence audits, ritual setup, repair under pressure, social bargaining, or survival challenges. Tool proficiencies can help, but no separate tradeskill subsystem is required.

A character can sense that an item is extraordinary by handling it. Identify or focused short-rest study can reveal properties. Dangerous Belavadös artifacts should reveal motives and costs through scenes, not only item rules.

Use attunement for items that change the bearer, stack major combat/social power, grant ongoing spell-like effects, or bind to a curse. Artifacts in these hooks are usually story objects; purified remnants can become rare, very rare, legendary, or artifact-tier rewards if the DM wants.
Level 8 is the campaign floor. Low fieldwork fits levels 8-9, moderate 9-11, high 10-12, severe 12-14, and extreme 14-16 unless the quest itself states otherwise.
Use reputation, permits, lodging, warrants, witnesses, safehouse access, transit priority, rare contacts, and legal leverage. Money and magic items are optional, not the only reward.
The four axes are reputation levers rather than punishment. Altruism, Lawfulness, Cooperation, and Honor should move based on visible choices and who benefits or suffers.

heading_path.heading_1: Artifact Logic for Belavadös
Artifact Logic for Belavadös

source_document_blocks.text: Artifacts in this setting do not need to be ornate. A broken mirror, pipe, rope, unfinished manuscript, ring, journal, suit of armor, or tool can become an artifact when a sacrifice, oath, murder, miracle, dragon-breath, lich-ritual, god-prison tremor, or perfectly witnessed moment catches inside it.

Hook: Sylvarielle Harbor Compact asks the party to secure rare materials, observations, witnesses, or ward components near Sylvarielle. This is no longer a crafting errand; it is a 5e expedition where survival choices, permits, and endangered workers matter. Objective: Use ability checks, tool proficiencies, spells, and roleplay to retrieve the objective without turning local laborers into bait. The material focus is masonry, but success should come from player choices, not a separate tradeskill system. Complication: This is an escort-crafting job: NPC workers can finish the task faster if the party controls noise, light, fear, and morale 5e / reward: Run as a 5e group check: 3 successes before 2 failures for low/moderate, 5 before 3 for high/severe, plus initiative if the hazard becomes active. Reward: Field formula: Brasscap Mushroom Field Method. Convert this to 5e as a consumable boon, advantage on a future related check, temporary equipment access, a permit, faction favor, or a contact rather than a standalone crafting subsystem. Artifact or chassis: skill challenge, escort, hazardous exploration, negotiation, or set-piece fight A normal job becomes heroic because the party protects people, truth, and civic infrastructure while handling dangerous materials. Alignment: Honor +250 for truthful reporting; Altruism -250 if refugees or laborers are used as bait

source_document_blocks.text: BQ-016 - Senior Writ: Three Stations in One Night | Drakesylva, Aelvanyr | Severe (Level 12-14) | Patron: Drakesylva Tideglass Conclave | Deity/Pantheon: Marduthor | Deadline: use settlement clock and patron deadline. Hook: Drakesylva Tideglass Conclave asks the party to secure rare materials, observations, witnesses, or ward components near Drakesylva. This is no longer a crafting errand; it is a 5e expedition where survival choices, permits, and endangered workers matter. Objective: Use ability checks, tool proficiencies, spells, and roleplay to retrieve the objective without turning local laborers into bait. The material focus is armorsmithing, but success should come from player choices, not a separate tradeskill system. Complication: This is an escort-crafting job: NPC workers can finish the task faster if the party controls noise, light, fear, and morale. A direct fight is possible, but a clever crafting solution should reduce the encounter budget or remove one wave entirely 5e / reward: Run as a 5e group check: 3 successes before 2 failures for low/moderate, 5 before 3 for high/severe, plus initiative if the hazard becomes active. Reward: Field formula: Sun-Hymn Wax Field Method. Convert this to 5e as a consumable boon, advantage on a future related check, temporary equipment access, a permit, faction favor, or a contact rather than a standalone crafting subsystem. Artifact or chassis: skill challenge, escort, hazardous exploration, negotiation, or set-piece fight A normal job becomes heroic because the party protects people, truth, and civic infrastructure while handling dangerous materials. Alignment: Lawfulness +250 for legal permits; Cooperation +250 for shared credit with local guilds

It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely. Objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it. Complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage. 5e / reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 15; Arcana/Religion/History DC 16; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 17; crisis save DC 16. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into Root, Rail, and Sacred Right; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item. Artifact or chassis: wondrous item tied to nature, beasts, weather, or survival magic grown, shed, or blood-blessed by a beast, dragon, river, grove, or old wilderness oath; its omen is shaped by Asethyr, god of primal freedom, tribal rites, revelry, instinct, and untamed cultures. Alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

source_document_blocks.text: BAQ-A080 - Seal Ichor-Slick Ring of the Imprisoned Choir | Sylvéraith, Aelwynora | Level 8 (standard high-fantasy threat) | Patron: local civic, temple, or containment authority | Deity/Pantheon: Iskareth | Deadline: Valkhaday Horundar 24 sixth bell. Hook: Sylvéraith reports that Ichor-Slick Ring is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely. Objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it. Complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage. 5e / reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 14; Arcana/Religion/History DC 15; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 16; crisis save DC 15. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Armory of Soft Apocalypse; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item. Artifact or chassis: wearable wondrous item, ring, armor, or restraint; attunement recommended because the object changes the bearer bound by a bearer who sacrificed comfort, identity, or a name; its omen is shaped by Iskareth, primordial mother of beasts, fertility, instinct, and natural kinship. Alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

source_document_blocks.text: BAQ-A029 - Seal Fungal Cutlass of the Imprisoned Choir | Elaréth, Iazethas | Level 12 (hard regional threat) | Patron: local civic, temple, or containment authority | Deity/Pantheon: Freyseth | Deadline: Nebday Iskazunet 27 gravewatch. Hook: Elaréth reports that Fungal Cutlass is no longer behaving like an object. It is changing records, bodies, witnesses, or civic machinery in ways that make panic, worship, and black-market seizure equally likely. Objective: Trace the relic, identify who fed it ichor or devotion, decide whether it must be sealed, purified, bargained with, or exposed, then complete a multi-stage 5e skill challenge before a rival faction claims it. Complication: The artifact is evidence, weapon, witness, and temptation at once. Destroying it may save lives but erase proof; using it may solve the scene while adding curse debt, attunement risk, or divine-prison leakage. 5e / reward: Core checks: Investigation or Insight DC 18; Arcana/Religion/History DC 19; containment, exorcism, legal proof, or sabotage DC 20; crisis save DC 19. Reward: Faction favor, restricted access, a safe minor echo of the relic as a one-use boon, or a lead into The Armory of Soft Apocalypse; the full artifact should remain a story object unless the DM intentionally builds it as a rare-or-higher magic item. Artifact or chassis: hazardous weapon or wondrous armament; require attunement if the party is allowed to wield a purified remnant dragon-forged, war-priest-made, lich-claimed, or battlefield-born; its omen is shaped by Freyseth, mistress of crossroads, curses, planar mysteries, and supernatural bloodlines. Alignment: Reward Altruism for protecting people before property, Lawfulness for clean warrants and permits, Cooperation for shared credit, and Honor for truthful disclosure.

heading_path.heading_1: Named NPC Reference

rows: Faerie obsessive apprentice gatherer, guild errand-spark, and adorable disaster magnet (Or'lythae, El'dravire Riverrealm; pronouns: they/them). Use Qho as the recurring innocent instigator. They never ask for murder; they ask for samples, observations, permits, and proof that adults are overreacting.

Human field captain of the Thornwillow Guard and practical protector of dangerous supply routes (Sylvanreach, Eldermere; pronouns: she/her). Use Mira to turn guard work into rescue logistics, bridge repairs, patrol-map ethics, and civilian protection instead of simple monster hunting.

Ombrask Arcane Shade Militia commander specializing in evidence wards, midnight warrants, and containment logistics (Eldryssar, Vaelmyrith; pronouns: they/them). Use Veyl to make law, secrecy, and arcane evidence dangerous without making the party villains by default.

heading_path.heading_1: Faction Framework Reference
Faction Framework Reference

source_document_blocks.text: Faction quests work best when each faction has a public goal, a hidden truth, a reward it can provide, and a line it will cross. Use these as recurring pressure engines for the hooks above.

heading_path.heading_1: Faction Framework Reference

rows: Defend settlements, repair transit lifelines, and keep hungry gods from becoming excuses for tyranny.
Some cells quietly move refugees away from ichor debts and forged death-ledgers.
Protect Belavadös from rogue constructs, uncontrolled ichor engines, and divine-prison breaches.
Their purity laws hide a terror of created people and souls housed in engineered bodies.
Expose abusive ledgers, hide endangered witnesses, and free people mislabeled as property.
Some cells erase memories without consent when they decide secrecy matters more than personhood.
Solve plague, famine, and magical instability through regulated research.
Their clean laboratories hide personhood theft, forced replacement, and soul architecture experiments.
Recover stolen identities, solve murders, and protect people whose memories have been tampered with.
The Inquest sells sanitized memories to nobles when survival requires compromise.
Keep ocean settlements alive through fog seasons, monster migrations, and divine seal tremors.
Their old families know which lighthouse bells are actually prison alarms.
Protect people from surface collapse with regulated underground infrastructure.
Some experiments measure obedience, desperation, and ichor dependency more than safety.
Make profit, hold territory, and turn terror into spectacle.
The league is a recruitment mask for old god-cults and debtor armies.

D&D Beyond, Let’s Design an Adventure: Outlines and Frameworks

Used for cold-open hooks that pull players directly into action or crisis.
Used to add reusable clue/reveal logic for investigation, exploration, and social play.

heading_path.heading_1: Final Running Checklist
Final Running Checklist

source_document_blocks.text: • Open with a visible crisis, not a lore lecture.

heading_path.heading_1: Final Running Checklist

source_document_blocks.text: • Give three clue paths to every required conclusion.

heading_path.heading_1: Final Running Checklist

source_document_blocks.text: • Name the faction that benefits if the party does nothing.

heading_path.heading_1: Final Running Checklist

source_document_blocks.text: • Make the artifact useful, dangerous, and morally expensive.

heading_path.heading_1: Final Running Checklist

source_document_blocks.text: • Track consequences through NPCs, permits, rumors, transit, sanctuary access, and alignment axes.

heading_path.heading_1: Final Running Checklist

source_document_blocks.text: • Never make tool proficiency mandatory; let it grant advantage, alternate clues, reduced time, safer repairs, or better rewards.
